seo.title: About
seo.description: Altrazen is a software studio built around one idea: software should be written for the person who maintains it next, not just for the day it ships.

hero.heading: Building software got cheap. Running it did not.
hero.description: That gap is the reason this studio exists, and it shapes everything about how we work.

story.heading: Why we started
paragraphs: In a short space of time, the cost of producing working software collapsed. Better frameworks, better hosting and AI coding assistants turned what used to take a small team a season into something one determined person can do in a fortnight. That is a genuinely good change, and the people taking advantage of it are not cutting corners.

But nothing made software cheaper to run. Backups still have to exist and be tested. Credentials still have to stay out of public repositories. Somebody still has to be told when the system goes down. Dependencies still need patching. None of that got faster, and none of it is what the tools are optimised to produce.

So there is now an enormous amount of software in production — real customers, real revenue — sitting on foundations nobody has ever inspected. And there is a second problem underneath it: even software that was built carefully tends to become unmaintainable, because it was written for the launch and not for the person who inherits it eighteen months later.
Altrazen was built around both halves. We write software for the next developer rather than for the demo, and we take over the systems where that did not happen.

mission.heading: Mission
mission.statement: To build software that the people who inherit it can understand, change and rely on — and to rescue the software where that was never true.

vision.heading: Vision
vision.statement: To be the engineering studio teams call when the work has to be right: for what they are building next, and for what they have already built and can no longer trust.

values.heading: Five values, each with a cost
values.description: A value that never changes a decision is decoration. Each of these has turned down work, extended a timeline or lost us money.

items.title: Honest over impressive
items.description: If your codebase is fine we tell you it is fine and do not sell you an audit. If a rewrite is the right answer we say so, even when the patch would have been our invoice. A report that inflates severity to justify a fee is worth nothing to you, and we will not write one.

items.title: Ownership, not tickets
items.description: When something breaks, the answer is never that it was outside scope. Someone owns your system end to end and follows a problem to wherever it actually lives, including into the parts nobody assigned them.

items.title: Boring technology wins
items.description: We reach for the least interesting solution that works. A well-placed index beats a new service almost every time. We will not introduce a technology into your stack because we wanted to learn it.

items.title: Document everything
items.description: If only one person understands how something works, that is a defect we introduced. Every change comes with a written record of what and why, so you are never held hostage by knowledge only we have — including on the day you decide to leave.

items.title: Say no early
items.description: We turn down work we are not right for on the first call rather than three weeks in. Saying no on Monday is a short conversation. Saying it after taking your money is a different thing entirely.

howWeWork.heading: The rules we actually apply
items: Small, reviewable pull requests. Nobody should have to read a two-thousand-line diff to know what changed.
Nothing ships without a way to undo it, and the rollback is tested before launch rather than during an incident.
Tests where a failure costs money — payment, authentication, data writes — rather than tests chasing a coverage number.
Secrets never touch the repository, in any branch, at any point in history.
Every alert reaches a person. An alert that only lands on a dashboard is not monitoring.
Accessibility to WCAG 2.2 AA is a build requirement, checked in CI, not a phase that gets cut when the date slips.
Architecture decisions that are expensive to reverse get written down with their reasoning.
Clients hear about problems we caused immediately, in plain language, with what we are doing about them.

team.heading: Who you'll work with
team.description: A small engineering team, growing carefully. The people who talk to you are the people who write the code — there is no account manager in between.

emptyState.heading: Profiles are being written
emptyState.description: We are growing, and rather than fill this section with stock photographs and invented titles we would rather leave it until the profiles are real. If you want to know exactly who would work on your project, ask on the first call and we will tell you.

cta.heading: Work with us
cta.description: Start with a conversation. We will tell you honestly whether we are the right studio for what you need.
